## A real terminal, folder-wide search, split editor groups, and a quieter idle window

Builds on **0.1.36**, which fixed Explorer rename and the Save / Don't Save dialog keys. This release rebuilds the integrated terminal, makes search and Quick Open cover the whole folder, gives each split editor group its own tab bar, and cuts the CPU an idle window uses.

### Integrated terminal
- The terminal is a real VT emulator: cursor moves, clears and the alternate screen work, so `vim`, `less` and `top` run full screen and give the transcript back when they exit. Scrollback keeps 5,000 lines and `stty size` matches the panel.
- ANSI colours (16 colours from VS Code's terminal palette, the 256-colour cube and truecolor), bold, italic, underline, dim and inverse video.
- Keys go straight to the shell: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+D, Tab, the arrows, Esc and the F-keys reach the program, so `sleep 30` or `yes` stop at once, Ctrl+D ends `cat` or `python`, Tab completes and Up recalls history. App shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+…, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+`, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Q) keep working.
- After Ctrl+C the screen lands on the prompt almost at once (typically 10–90 ms), even during a flood of output.
- Heavy output no longer freezes the window: reading and parsing happen off the UI thread, sustained floods are throttled and repainted less often, and memory stays flat. `yes` uses well under one core.
- Clicking in the output and then typing always reaches the shell.
- Terminal tabs work like VS Code's terminal groups: **New Terminal** (+) starts a tab of its own, and **Split** divides only the current tab, beside the active terminal. Before, + then Split could lose a terminal session; now every session keeps running. The tab strip is always shown, so the header buttons don't move when you add a tab.
- VS Code's panel actions in the header: New (+), Split (also Ctrl+Shift+5), Kill, Maximize / Restore and Close Panel, next to Copy, Paste and Clear.
- The panel opens at a third of the window, and its height is remembered when you drag the divider.
- Shells load your rc files by default (the new **Terminal Loads Shell Config** setting turns that off). With `$SHELL` unset, Malgel uses your login shell instead of `/bin/sh`.
- Closing or killing a terminal never blocks the window, a shell's last output is no longer lost when it exits, and opening the panel from a file in another folder no longer restarts a busy shell.

### Keyboard focus
- When the focused element goes away (for example Ctrl+2, a click on the preview, then Ctrl+1), keys no longer go dead until the next mouse click: focus returns to the active editor and the key is replayed there.

### Search and Quick Open
- Find in Files, Replace All and Quick Open now cover every file in the folder. Before, they saw only the first 4,000 files in no fixed order, so a big folder could report "No matches" or get a partial Replace All.
- The Search view counts every match. It shows at most 1,000 rows per file and 10,000 in total, and the header gives the true totals (for example "80002 results in 20001 files — showing 10000"). Each file's badge counts all of its matches.
- Ctrl+Shift+F and Ctrl+Shift+H open the Search view: Enter runs the search, then Enter / Shift+Enter step through the hits, and Escape goes back to the editor. **Ctrl+Alt+Enter** runs Replace All, as in VS Code.
- Quick Open rows show the file name in bold, its folder smaller and dimmed, and the letters you typed highlighted. Large folders no longer cost hundreds of MiB while Quick Open is open.

### Split Editor
- Ctrl+\ opens a second view of the current file beside it, as VS Code does. Both views edit the same file, and each keeps its own caret.
- Each editor group has its own tab bar: side by side, each column has its own tabs; with Split Down, the lower pane has one too.
- Closing one of two views of a file with unsaved changes closes it at once, keeping your edits in the other view. Malgel asks to save only when the last view closes, and saving one view marks the others saved.
- Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch tabs only within the group that has the keyboard. Before, Ctrl+Tab in one group could leave it blank while your typing went into a document you couldn't see. Going to the other group's document moves the keyboard there, and closing a tab never leaves both groups showing the same document.
- Ctrl+Shift+T puts a reopened tab back where it was.

### Explorer
- Enter opens the selected file on Linux and Windows (F2 renames), and renames on macOS, as in VS Code. Enter on a folder still opens or closes it.
- The row the arrow keys move from has a focus ring while the Explorer has the keyboard.

### Idle CPU
- The caret stops blinking after 10 seconds of no input (as GTK does) and starts again with the next key, click or refocus. Every blink repainted the whole window.
- The status bar's memory and CPU figures only repaint when they really change, so an idle window no longer repaints forever.

### Performance gate
- `scripts/e2e/perf_scenes.sh` measures first frame, editor and terminal input latency, Ctrl+C to prompt, peak memory and idle CPU (with and without focus) from outside the app. It fails when a median goes over budget, and runs in CI as **perf gate (Linux)**. CI also runs a terminal stress job. Focused idle CPU (measured once the caret has stopped blinking) is reported but does not fail the gate yet.
- Windows test builds work again (the PTY session tests are Unix only).
### Verify
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `scripts/e2e/gui_smoke.sh`
- `scripts/e2e/terminal_stress.sh`
- `scripts/e2e/perf_scenes.sh`
